kanban-claude 0.2.0.dev10

The /kanban-board pane now opens on a card view: each lane is a column of bordered cards, and a need that waits on you is a card of its own. v switches to the old list. This page explains what changed and why.

Release explainer, 2026-10-20. Diff v0.2.0.dev9 (65af0cd) to b71e070 (feature/pane-cards). Dev pre-release. The version bump to 0.2.0.dev10 is still uncommitted, so it is not part of this diff.

  • 2

    commits: the card view, and the merge fix text (a docs-only fix to the dev9 page rode along in the range)

  • 7

    files changed (not counting the dev9 page and this one)

  • +326
    −31

    lines added and removed (git diff --shortstat v0.2.0.dev9...HEAD -- . ':!docs')

  • 29

    pane test cases in board.test.ts, ten of them new; no schema change, no new config key

Background

What was wrong with the pane, and what the owner asked for

The pane (plugins/kanban-claude/hooks/board.tsx) is the board beside the transcript, opened with /kanban-board. dev8 reworked it as a list: a needs-you strip, a health line, and one row per card in each lane. The owner opened it on a live board and found three things hard.

  • The needs-you item for a failed merge read as a raw code line: approval_not_clean → kanban merge-retry t_7ce189f8.
  • The sections ran together.
  • Nothing said that the pane's hotkeys only work after it gets the keyboard. v and r typed into the prompt instead; that happened during testing.

He asked for two selectable views and prefers the card view. dev10 makes cards the default and keeps the list behind v. It also fixes a gap on the runtime side that the new needs card made visible: a card whose PR the owner merged by hand stayed in Needs you. The board, its database and the config keys do not change. Line numbers are in plugins/kanban-claude/hooks/board.tsx at b71e070 unless a path says otherwise.

Change diagram

Which components changed, and how

  • + added
  • ~ changed
  • = left as it was

Arrows show how the pane feeds itself when it draws. The view state picks cards or list, the card view draws the needs and the lanes, the footer comes with it, and the tests check all of it. The merge fix text has no arrow: it is runtime text in a card comment, and the pane builds its own command line in ask(). Every item is explained in the walkthrough.

Render

The dock on a scratch board

This is a 57-cell dock captured from tmux on a scratch board, redrawn here with approximate colours. Lane borders are dim in the lane's colour: Running green, Review purple, Blocked red, Up next blue. The needs-you border is amber. The two blocks show the same board in the card view and, after v, in the list view.

In the card capture the pane has no keyboard, so the footer shows ctrl+x tab: keys. The list capture was taken with the pane focused, so its footer shows the hotkeys. The merge item shows the reason in words and the command on its own line. Up next holds four cards, and the dock's height allowed two, so it ends in +2 more.

Walkthrough

Area by area

Each area says what changed, why, and how you notice it as the operator.

The lanes become columns of cards +added~changed

What changed
In the dock, board.tsx:707 adds a branch for view === 'cards'. Running, Review, Blocked and Up next are columns of cards. Each card is a Box with a round border in the lane's theme colour, drawn dim and bright on hover. Inside it are the priority badge (only when the priority is above 0) with the first title line, one more title line if needed, and a dim meta line from the lane: owner and age, PR and age, or the block kind. wrap() (:103) word-wraps the title into at most two lines; the last line ends in an ellipsis when the title is longer. The first title line is a Button, so focus and Enter open the card's detail. The border sits on the Box around it, because a Button holds only text (tile, :736). Columns: as many across as fit at CARD_MIN = 22 cells plus a 2-cell gap (:712), at most four. perRow (:713) then spreads the four lanes evenly over the rows they need: a 57-cell dock fits two across, so two rows of two; a 120-column inline pane fits all four in one row. A card's text gets four cells less than its column (border and padding). A lane with no card keeps its place: its head is drawn in the inactive colour with a dash under it. A board with no cards in any lane still says Nothing running or planned. once.
Why
The owner looked at the old pane on a live board and found it hard to read: the sections ran together, and a failed merge showed as a raw code line. He asked for two views and prefers the cards. This comes from his request; the diff records the mechanism, not the motive.
How you notice it
The pane opens on cards. A title that does not fit in two lines ends in an ellipsis. cards are the default: each lane a column of bordered cards, two lanes across a 48-column dock checks the border, the width (23), the wrapped second line (backoff configurab…) and which lanes share a row. an empty lane keeps its place in the card grid, drawn faint checks the dash and the colour, and inline and wide, the four lanes of cards sit side by side, as many cards as the frame holds checks the 120-column layout.

Cards a lane come from the pane's height +added

What changed
room starts at CARDS = 3 and drops by one while the frame is too short, but never below 1 (:733). The frame test is above + tall(room) > scroll.bodyRows. above counts the rows around the lanes: the header, bar and footer, the stale line, the need cards and Merged. tall(k) counts, for each row of lanes, one blank row, the lane head, the tallest column of k cards (a card is its two border rows, its title lines and its meta line) and one row for +N more when some lane has more. Whatever does not fit shows as +N more under the lane, in dim italic. So the footer, with its keys, stays in view.
Why
A fixed number of cards would push the footer off a short pane, and the footer is where the keys are.
How you notice it
the dock shows as many cards per lane as its height holds, so the footer stays in view gives Up next eight cards. At 80 rows the test expects three shown and +5 more; at 34 rows it expects one shown and +7 more.

v switches between cards and list, and the choice is kept +added=frozen

What changed
A new view atom (:26) holds 'cards' or 'list'; null reads as cards. flip() (:334) swaps the two, updates the atom and writes the value to $.store, ignoring a failed write. At session start (:373) the pane reads the store and takes the value only if it is cards or list. types/index.d.ts adds view: 'cards' | 'list' | null to the declared atoms. The key is not per folder: a comment on flip says the look should follow the person into every folder, unlike the reopen key. The footer button shows the other view's name, so it reads v: list in cards and v: cards in the list. The list view is the old rendering, kept as it was: lanes side by side from 72 columns inline, stacked otherwise. The one edit there is that used, the row count both views need, moved out of the inline branch.
Why
Two views for two tastes, and a pane that reopens in the one you picked rather than asking again.
How you notice it
v switches to the list and back, and the next session opens on the view picked last presses the button twice, reads the store each time, then starts a new session with list saved and expects the list. The old list tests now press v first, for example the list view draws the lanes with their meta, the bar and the legend.

Needs-you items are cards ~changed=frozen

What changed
In the dock, each need (up to CARDS = 3, then +N more) is a Box with a round border in the warning colour (:766). The top line holds the label, bold and fit to 10 cells, and the title; it is a Button that opens the card when the need has a task id, and plain text when it has none. Under it come the reason, dim, on its own line, and the command, bold, on the next line after →. To make that possible ask() (:133) now returns why and act separately. It still returns hint, the two joined, which the list view uses. A need with no reason still shows its command as act. For merge_failed the reason now goes through words(), so approval_not_clean reads approval not clean; before, the pane showed approval_not_clean → kanban merge-retry t_7ce189f8 on one line. Inline from 72 columns the card view still draws the existing needs strip (strip(2, true)).
Why
A reason and a command read as one code line are easy to miss, and the command is the thing the owner has to copy. Each now has its own line, and the border says this is the part that waits on you.
How you notice it
each need is a card on top: the ask, the reason, then the command on its own line checks the border colour, the label and title in the button, and pressing it opens the detail. a failed merge reads in words, with the retry on its own line checks both texts. a need with no reason still shows its command as the action checks that the command is bold. the list keeps the needs-you strip: the reason, and the command whole on its own line checks that the list still works.

The footer says when the keys work, and the sections get air ~changed+added

What changed
The footer (:603) shows the v and refresh buttons only when e.props.isFocused is true. Otherwise it shows a dim ctrl+x tab: keys. The same footer serves both views. In the card view the dock also gets blank rows: before Needs you (:767), before each row of lanes (:803), before Merged (:815) and before the footer (:819). Inline and wide, where height is short, those rows are not added (lift is 0). The diff adds no spacing to the list view. The test helper pane() now defaults to isFocused: true, so the other tests see the hotkeys.
Why
A pane receives hotkeys only while it holds the keyboard. Before that, v and r type into the prompt, and the old footer showed them as if they were armed. That happened during testing. The blank rows answer the other complaint, that the sections ran together.
How you notice it
an unfocused pane says how to reach its keys instead of showing keys that would land in the prompt mounts the pane unfocused and expects the hint text and no view button. Click the pane, or press Ctrl+X then Tab, and the footer changes to the hotkeys.

A PR merged by hand now comes with a retry hint ~changed

What changed
Two entries in the FIX dict of housekeeping.py changed. approval_not_clean (:29) now reads merge the PR on GitHub if you accept it, then run: kanban merge-retry {id}; or have it reviewed again with: kanban reopen-review {id} --reason TEXT. base_is_default (:33) now reads …merge it on GitHub, or retarget it; then run: kanban merge-retry {id}. This is the text of the comment the failed merge leaves on the card. The other entries are unchanged.
Why
A merge that fails on one of these two reasons leaves the card with merge_state failed. If the owner then merged the PR on GitHub, nothing told him to retry, so the card stayed in Needs you. merge_retry (store.py:1398) puts a failed merge back to pending, and the merge job reads the PR. It checks for state MERGED before it checks the preconditions (housekeeping.py:136-141), so a PR merged by hand settles the card as merged without another merge call.
How you notice it
The comment now ends in the retry command, and the pane's merge card already shows → kanban merge-retry <id>. merge-retry refuses a card unless it is done with a failed merge. FIXES in test_merge.py:87 expects the new text; test_v1_each_precondition_fails_closed_and_names_itself checks it for base_is_default and test_p05_the_guard_still_refuses_a_partial_summary_and_names_its_own_fix for approval_not_clean.

Upgrade notes

Moving from dev9 to dev10

  1. Run the setup skill: /kanban-claude:setup. The diff changes no table and no config key, so there is no migration. The merge fix text is written by the daemon, so the daemon has to run the new version; the setup restarts it, as for dev9.
  2. With nothing saved, the pane opens on cards. Press v for the list. The choice is stored under the plugin's view key.
  3. A merge-failure comment already on a card keeps the text it was written with. For a card stuck in Needs you after you merged its PR on GitHub, run kanban merge-retry <id>.

Range covered

The diff runs from the tag v0.2.0.dev9 to b71e070: 203f8d2 (the card view), b71e070 (the merge fix text), and a docs-only fix to the dev9 page (9c3c1f2, merged in 727af30) that makes its diff stat wrap on two deliberate lines. The README and current_state.md ship in the same range. The version bump to 0.2.0.dev10, with its CHANGELOG entry, is in the working tree and not in this diff.

Quiz

Check what you took from this page

Five questions. Pick an answer to see the explanation.

1. What decides how many cards a lane shows in the dock?

room starts at 3 and drops while above + tall(room) is more than bodyRows (board.tsx:733). The rest shows as +N more.

2. The footer reads ctrl+x tab: keys. What does it tell you?

The hotkey buttons are drawn only when e.props.isFocused is true (board.tsx:603). Click the pane, or press Ctrl+X then Tab, to get them.

3. You press v in one folder, then start a session in another. Which view opens?

flip() writes view to $.store, and the session start reads it back (board.tsx:334, :373). It is not tied to a folder, unlike the reopen key.

4. A card shows approval not clean in Needs you, and you merged its PR on GitHub. What do you run?

The new fix text says so. merge_retry sets the merge back to pending, and the job checks for MERGED first (housekeeping.py:136-141).

5. A need has no reason. What does its card show?

ask() returns why and act apart, and the card draws each only when it is not empty. The test a need with no reason still shows its command as the action checks the bold command.
